claim.claim-text: 1. A closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100), comprising: a thermal preheating reservoir (102) configured to receive an external waste-heat flux and elevate an aqueous working fluid to an operating temperature of approximately 90°C; a hydrodynamic cavitation chamber (104) lined with chemical-vapor-deposition (CVD) graphene (106) and coupled to the thermal preheating reservoir (102), configured to induce acoustic and hydrodynamic micro-bubble collapse within the preheated aqueous working fluid; a nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (108) driven by a zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) high-voltage pulse generator (110) operating at approximately 33.6 kV, configured to dissociate cavitated vapor into reactive radical species and mineralize dissolved contaminants; an oil-free gas-bearing opposed-piston free-piston linear alternator (112) having 5-micrometer aerodynamic clearances (114) and permanent-magnet translators (116), configured to convert thermal-plasma expansion into continuous alternating electrical power; and a cold-sink condenser loop (118) configured to reject low-grade heat to an external heat sink and recover sterile distilled water (120) in a closed loop.

2. The closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100) of claim 1, wherein the CVD graphene lining (106) reduces the acoustic cavitation inception threshold pressure such that hydrodynamic cavitation power draw is maintained below 22.0 W per core.

3. The closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100) of claim 1, wherein the external waste-heat flux provides at least 382.93 Wth of sensible and latent enthalpy offset per core at 90°C to reduce internal electrical heating demand.

4. The closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100) of claim 1, further comprising a solid-oxide yttria-stabilized zirconia (8YSZ) oxygen-ion separation membrane (122) coupled downstream of the nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (108) to extract medical-grade gaseous oxygen (124).

5. The closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100) of claim 1, wherein the nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (108) cleaves carbon-fluorine (C-F) bonds of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) with a destruction and removal efficiency (DRE) of at least 99.9999% (6-Log) and precipitates inert calcium fluoride (CaF2) mineral solids (126).

6. The closed-loop thermo-chemical power and fluid-regeneration core (100) of claim 1, further comprising a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) electronic control unit (128) consuming less than 15.0 W and regulating ZVS pulse frequency (110) and linear alternator (112) phase synchronization.

7. A modular containerized skid comprising a plurality of closed-loop cores (100) of claim 1 manifolded in parallel across a common waste-heat header, a cold-sink condenser header (118), and a direct-current microgrid bus.

8. A radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400), comprising: a pressure-containment shell (402) enclosing a radionuclide concentration sump (404) coupled to a 90°C CVD-graphene hydrodynamic cavitation stage (104) and a 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (108); an array of chemical-vapor-deposition (CVD) diamond-passivated 4H-silicon carbide (4H-SiC) betavoltaic tiles (406) lining an interior wet wall of the radionuclide concentration sump (404) to convert beta-particle emission into direct electrical current; a hafnium-oxide/tantalum-oxide (HfO2/Ta2O5) and CVD-graphene Schottky gamma-voltaic liner (408) surrounding the radionuclide concentration sump (404) to convert incident gamma photons into electrical power; a graded tungsten-boron carbide (W-B4C) gamma-attenuation shield (410) enveloping the gamma-voltaic liner (408); and a bismuth-telluride/lead-magnesium-niobate-lead-titanate (Bi2Te3/PMN-PT) thermoelectric collar (412) thermally bridging the W-B4C gamma-attenuation shield (410) to an external cold sink (118).

9. The radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400) of claim 8, wherein ionizing radiation from concentrated cesium-137, strontium-90, and tritium generates radiolytic hydroxyl radicals within the aqueous working fluid to lower 33.6 kV ZVS plasma excitation power draw below 16.0 W.

10. The radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400) of claim 8, wherein the graded W-B4C gamma-attenuation shield (410) attenuates at least 99.4% of incident gamma flux while converting absorbed gamma energy into thermal energy harvested by the thermoelectric collar (412).

11. The radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400) of claim 8, further comprising a palladium-silver (Pd-Ag) permeation membrane (414) configured to separate and enrich tritiated hydrogen isotopes (HTO/T2) from distilled water vapor (120).

12. The radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400) of claim 8, further comprising a pneumatic vitrified-cake discharge gate (416) at a base of the radionuclide concentration sump (404) achieving a solid waste volume reduction ratio exceeding 10,000:1.

13. The radiation-harvesting nuclear remediation core (400) of claim 8, wherein permanent magnets (116) of the linear alternator (112) comprise samarium-cobalt (Sm2Co17) and control electronics comprise radiation-hardened silicon-on-insulator (SOI) circuitry (502) rated to at least 10^8 Gy total ionizing dose.

14. A wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600), comprising: a liquid cooling garment (LCG) (602) worn by an operator and thermally coupled to a 90°C preheating reservoir (604) to transfer metabolic waste heat into a closed-loop fluid-regeneration circuit; a micro-cavitation chamber lined with CVD graphene (606) and a 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (608) configured to sterilize operator perspiration, urine condensate, and exhaled carbon dioxide into potable water (610) and breathable oxygen (612); an oil-free linear alternator (614) and a graphene supercapacitor bank (616) forming a 48 V bidirectional direct-current power bus (702); and a multi-axis quasi-direct-drive (QDD) brushless exoskeleton frame (704) powered by the 48 V bidirectional direct-current power bus (702) and configured to capture regenerative braking energy during eccentric limb motion.

15. The wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600) of claim 14, further comprising a Sabatier and catalytic pyrolysis carbon trap (618) configured to reduce exhaled carbon dioxide into solid graphitic carbon (620) and closed-loop water without consumable chemical scrubbers.

16. The wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600) of claim 14, wherein the multi-axis QDD brushless exoskeleton frame (704) comprises 6 lower-body degrees of freedom and 4 upper-body manipulator degrees of freedom (706) shunting external payload forces directly to ground contact boots (708).

17. The wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600) of claim 14, further comprising a 48 V electrical power take-off (PTO) port (710) and a pressurized sterile-air/ozonated-water fluidic PTO port (712) for powering external rescue tools.

18. The wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600) of claim 14, wherein the cold-sink condenser (118) rejects heat to an ambient planetary or deep-sea environment to sustain sealed life support for at least 368 continuous hours.

19. The wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system (600) of claim 14, further comprising an electrodynamic dust shield (EDS) (714) energized by the 33.6 kV pulse generator (608) across rotary joint seals to repel lunar or Martian regolith dust.

20. An autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800), comprising: a reconfigurable articulated chassis (802) driven by quasi-direct-drive (QDD) brushless joint actuators (804); a liquid thermal-capture jacket (806) surrounding the QDD brushless joint actuators (804) to harvest actuator waste heat into a 90°C preheating reservoir (808); a micro-cool power core (810) having a CVD-graphene cavitation stage, a 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor, and a linear alternator generating continuous electrical power, sterile potable water (812), and breathable oxygen (814) for supported personnel; and articulated dorsal ballistic shield wings (902) fabricated from boron-carbide/ultra-high-molecular-weight-polyethylene (B4C/UHMWPE) composite and deployable within 0.30 seconds to form protective cover.

21. The autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800) of claim 20, wherein the reconfigurable articulated chassis (802) is selectively configurable among a quadruped hound morphology, an agile feline scout morphology, and a winged dragon morphology having attachable graphene-composite soaring membranes (904).

22. The autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800) of claim 20, further comprising a closed-loop 38.5°C thermoregulated affective outer skin (816) and biometric acoustic/heart-rate sensors (818) configured to provide physiological stabilization and mental-health companionship to isolated operators.

23. The autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800) of claim 20, further comprising a 2-degree-of-freedom articulated tail auger (820) coupled to the 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor to fix atmospheric nitrogen into nitrate-enriched planetary regolith during terraforming operations.

24. The autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800) of claim 20, wherein the dorsal ballistic shield wings (902) achieve National Institute of Justice (NIJ) Level IV ballistic protection upon deployment triggered by an onboard acoustic gunshot-localization array (906).

25. The autonomous multi-morphology biomimetic robotic platform (800) of claim 20, wherein the linear alternator (112) and graphene supercapacitor bank (616) provide continuous autonomous endurance exceeding 360 hours while hauling up to 65 kg in Earth gravity or 170 kg in Martian gravity.

26. A multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000), comprising: a plurality of autonomous robotic units (1002a, 1002b), each incorporating a micro-cool power core (810) having a 90°C thermal water reservoir (808), a 48 V bidirectional direct-current bus (702), and deployable ballistic shield wings (902); a magnetic self-aligning dry-break umbilical coupler (1004) mounted on each robotic unit (1002a, 1002b) and configured to mate peer-to-peer to transfer both 48 V electrical power (1006) and 90°C preheated working fluid (1008) between units; and an ultra-wideband (UWB) and sub-gigahertz mesh transceiver (1102) configured to synchronize relative positioning within 2 centimeters and command simultaneous deployment of the ballistic shield wings (902) into a continuous interlocking phalanx barrier (1104).

27. The multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000) of claim 26, wherein a donor robotic unit (1002a) executing high-exertion actuator tasks transfers surplus 90°C preheated water (1008) through the magnetic dry-break umbilical coupler (1004) to a stationary recipient robotic unit (1002b) to boost electrical generation without activating resistive heaters.

28. The multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000) of claim 26, wherein the interlocking phalanx barrier (1104) deploys within 0.35 seconds of an acoustic or optical threat detection to enclose supported personnel behind an overlapping NIJ Level IV shield wall.

29. The multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000) of claim 26, wherein the magnetic dry-break umbilical coupler (1004) includes dual-check poppet valves (1010) and hall-effect arc-free contactors (1012) rated for at least 1.2 kW continuous power transfer in dusty or submerged environments.

30. The multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000) of claim 26, further comprising an airborne winged dragon relay unit (1106) maintaining line-of-sight LoRa and UWB mesh backhaul across subterranean, urban, or Martian canyon terrain.

31. The multi-agent autonomous robotic swarm system (1000) of claim 26, wherein an onboard distributed auction controller (1014) allocates surplus electrical energy (1006), potable water (812), and gaseous oxygen (814) across swarm members based on real-time state-of-charge and mission priority.

32. A handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) for low-pressure planetary environments, comprising: a hilt housing (1202) enclosing a replaceable ice/water cartridge (1204), a 90°C thermal reservoir (1206), a CVD-graphene hydrodynamic cavitation stage (1208), a 33.6 kV ZVS pulsed plasma exciter (1210), and an oil-free linear alternator (1212); a composite emitter nozzle (1214) having a samarium-cobalt (Sm2Co17) Halbach permanent-magnet array (1216) and a water-cooled copper-chromium-zirconium (CuCrZr) Bitter electromagnet coil (1218) configured to project an elongated closed-loop toroidal plasma blade (1220) in an ambient Martian atmosphere at approximately 610 Pa; an external titanium-alloy cryogenic fin radiator (1222) thermally coupled to the hilt housing (1202) to reject condenser heat to a -60°C Martian ambient heat sink and regenerate continuous electrical power into a graphene supercapacitor bank (1302); and a capacitive extravehicular-activity (EVA) glove deadman sensor (1304) configured to de-energize the Bitter electromagnet coil (1218) within 1.2 milliseconds upon grip release.

33. The handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) of claim 32, wherein the Sm2Co17 Halbach array (1216) and CuCrZr Bitter electromagnet coil (1218) generate a peak throat magnetic flux density of at least 0.65 T and a distal magnetic mirror pinch of 0.67 T at a blade length of 0.92 meters.

34. The handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) of claim 32, further comprising a coaxial vapor aspiration shroud (1224) surrounding the emitter nozzle (1214) to recapture dissociated water and carbon-monoxide/oxygen ions back into the 90°C thermal reservoir (1206) for closed-loop endurance exceeding 75 hours per 180 mL cartridge.

35. The handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) of claim 32, wherein the external titanium-alloy cryogenic fin radiator (1222) and linear alternator (1212) generate at least 142.0 W of net continuous recharging power in a -60°C Martian environment.

36. The handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) of claim 32, wherein the capacitive EVA-glove deadman sensor (1304) triggers a solid-state gallium-nitride (GaN) crowbar dump circuit (1306) that collapses magnetic confinement and extinguishes the plasma blade (1220) within 1.2 milliseconds.

37. The handheld magneto-confined plasma lance system (1200) of claim 32, wherein the hilt housing (1202) has a dry mass not exceeding 2.48 kg and is selectively switchable among a permafrost core-boring mode, a structural metal/regolith welding mode, a basalt rock-cutting mode, and an emergency airlock breach-rescue mode.

38. A deep-sea hydrothermal plasma torch system (1400) operable at hydrostatic pressures up to 60.8 MPa, comprising: a pressure-compensated titanium-alloy housing (1402) enclosing a 90°C thermal reservoir (1404), a CVD-graphene hydrodynamic cavitation chamber (1406), a 33.6 kV ZVS pulsed plasma generator (1408), and an oil-free linear alternator (1410); a coaxial water-swirl plasma nozzle (1412) surrounded by a 0.75 T Sm2Co17 magnetic confinement collar (1414) configured to project a hydro-sheathed 6,800 K plasma cutting jet (1416) into ambient seawater; a double-walled arc-shroud heat recuperator (1418) transferring plasma plume waste heat back into the 90°C thermal reservoir (1404); and a hull-conformal condenser (1420) rejecting heat to 2°C abyssal seawater to regenerate at least 196.4 W of continuous electrical power into a graphene supercapacitor bank (1422).

39. The deep-sea hydrothermal plasma torch system (1400) of claim 38, further comprising a rotary diver/ROV deadman hall-effect switch (1424) configured to quench the 33.6 kV ZVS pulsed plasma generator (1408) and close a seawater isolation valve within 1.0 millisecond.

40. The deep-sea hydrothermal plasma torch system (1400) of claim 38, wherein the coaxial water-swirl plasma nozzle (1412) operates continuously at depths down to 6,000 meters without surface umbilical power or compressed gas cylinders.

41. A microgravity asteroid plasma rock-splitter system (1500), comprising: a chassis (1502) enclosing a 90°C thermal reservoir (1504), a CVD-graphene cavitation stage (1506), a 33.6 kV ZVS plasma generator (1508), and a linear alternator (1510); a magnetic-mirror plasma needle emitter (1512) having a 0.58 T pinch throat configured to project a focused 5,400 K plasma beam (1514) into asteroid regolith to flash-vaporize bound phyllosilicate water and induce internal tensile spallation with less than 0.15 N of axial recoil force; an electrostatic-and-cryogenic volatile capture hood (1516) surrounding the target zone to aspirate released water vapor, carbon dioxide, and metal-carbonyl gases back into the 90°C thermal reservoir (1504); and a shaded deep-space radiator (1518) rejecting heat at approximately 120 K to regenerate at least 184.0 W of continuous electrical power.

42. The microgravity asteroid plasma rock-splitter system (1500) of claim 41, wherein recovered phyllosilicate water vapor from C-type carbonaceous asteroid regolith replenishes the 90°C thermal reservoir (1504) at a net positive mass balance exceeding 100% of plasma propellant consumption.

43. The microgravity asteroid plasma rock-splitter system (1500) of claim 41, further comprising a catalytic carbonyl-cracking trap (1520) coupled to the volatile capture hood (1516) to deposit pure nickel and iron powders from aspirated metal-carbonyl vapors during M-type asteroid mining.
